headline: NAB's APRA Level 2 Group CET1 ratio declined 65 bps over FY25, from 12.35% at September 2024 to 11.70% at September 2025. The reduction was driven by lending volume growth increasing RWA, increased long-term investment in the business, and a $0.6 billion share buy-back (-15 bps). Cash earnings were broadly stable at $7,091m (FY24: $7,102m). CET1 capital rose modestly by $388m to $51,527m, while total RWA grew 6.4% to $440.6bn. Pro forma CET1 ratio was 11.81%, reflecting the MLC Life sale completed in October 2025. No full-year CET1 walk chart is published; the bank provides only a half-on-half walk (Mar 25 to Sep 25, -31 bps).

drivers.narrative: The Group completed its $3.0 billion on-market ordinary share buy-back on 12 March 2025, of which $0.6 billion (16.6 million shares) was bought back in FY25, reducing CET1 capital by 0.15% or 15 bps.

Credit RWA increased from $350.9bn to $375.0bn (+6.9%), driven by business lending growth (B&PB business lending balances rose 7.3%, C&IB lending grew 11.8%) and home lending balances growing 5.2%. A $4.8bn RWA overlay for off-balance sheet exposures was introduced in Sep 25 (Mar 25 and Sep 24: nil). The bank does not disclose a specific bpts impact for volume growth on the CET1 ratio over the full year.

Total dividends for FY25 were 170 cps (interim 85 cps + final 85 cps), 1 cp higher than FY24 (169 cps). The payout ratio was 73.3% of cash earnings. The half-on-half walk shows dividend at -61 bps for Mar 25 to Sep 25. The bank does not disclose a specific bpts impact for the full-year dividend on the CET1 ratio.

Investment spend increased by $147m or 9.0% to $1.8bn in FY25 (FY24: $1.6bn), covering infrastructure ($609m), compliance and risk ($587m), and customer experience/efficiency ($589m). This reflects ongoing technology modernisation, branch network refresh, cyber security, and lending platform investments. The bank does not quantify this as a specific bpts impact on CET1.

Cash earnings were broadly stable at $7,091m (FY24: $7,102m), down 0.2%. CET1 capital increased by $388m to $51,527m. The half-on-half walk shows cash earnings contributing +82 bps for Mar 25 to Sep 25. The bank does not disclose a specific bpts impact for earnings on the full-year CET1 movement.

disagreements.explanation: The internationally comparable CET1 ratio (12.1% Sep 24, 11.7% Sep 25 per investor presentation p106) excludes the APRA capital floor adjustment and uses Basel III methodology. The task requires the APRA Level 2 Group CET1 ratio (12.35% Sep 24, 11.70% Sep 25 per results book p30).

limitations: No full-year (FY24 to FY25) CET1 ratio walk chart is published by NAB. Only a half-on-half walk (Mar 25 to Sep 25, -31 bps) is provided, which cannot be used as the task comparison.

Only the share buy-back driver is quantified by the bank at -15 bps for the full year. All other drivers (volume growth, investment, earnings, dividend) are described narratively without specific bpts impacts for the FY24-FY25 period.

The residual of -35 bps represents unquantified drivers including FX translation, model/methodology changes, asset quality deterioration, and other miscellaneous items that the bank does not break out for the full year.

The half-on-half walk bars (cash earnings +82 bps, dividend -61 bps, credit RWA -45 bps, other RWA +1 bps, other -8 bps) describe a different comparison period and cannot be attributed to the FY24-FY25 movement.

evidence_records.quote: The Group CET1 ratio was 11.70% at September 2025 compared with our target of greater than 11.25% and declined 65 bps over the year with key drivers including volume growth, increased long term investment in the business, and completion of the on-market share buy-back(9). Adjusting for finalisation of the MLC Life sale(10), proforma Group CET1 is 11.81%.

Group CET1 ratio of 11.70%, down (65 bps) from September 2024. Key drivers of the reduction include lending volume growth, increased long term investment in the business and the impact of $0.6 billion of shares bought back in FY25 (-15 bps)(1)

Through this buy-back, the Group has bought back and cancelled 87,824,707 ordinary shares, including 16,572,039 ordinary shares ($0.6 billion or 0.15% of CET1 capital) in the September 2025 full year.
